To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reflection of an obliquely incident electromagnetic wave by a lossy isotropic dielectric slab can be controlled by a Pockels cover without depolarization.

the reflection from an isotropic, loss dielectric slab backed with a perfect electric conductor is electrically switchable by covering the slab with a thin epitaxial layer made of a cubic noncentrosymmetry material that displays the Pockels electro-optic effect.
the Pockels-effect cover can be used to electrically control the reflection from a lossy, grounded dielectric slab in mid- and long-wavelength infrared regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an electrically switchable, broadband, polarization-insensitive, infrared reflectance modulator based on the Pockels-effect-induced birefringence.
the switchable control of infrared reflectance by a grounded, lossy, dielectric slab with the aid of a Pockels cover.
the design, analysis, and optimization of a novel Pockels cover for electrically switchable control of reflection from a grounded dielectric slab.

, the proposed Pockels cover is a promising candidate for the realization of switchable control of obliquely reflected waves by lossy, isotropy dielectric slabs, and can be applied to the design of infrared optical devices, including polarization-insensitive infrared detectors and infrared polarizers, etc.
the Pockels covers are capable of electrically switching the reflection of oblique incidence light with any polarization state by a lossy dielectric layer backed by a perfect conductor.
the proposed Pockels cover can be utilized as a switchable control of reflection from the dielectric slab.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reflection can be switched between the maximum and minimum values, and the polarization states of the reflected waves can be changed by the Pockels covers.

the Pockels-effect-based electric-field control of the infrared reflection from the lossy, isotopic, dielectric slab can be realized by the Pockels-cover design, without the use of the metal or semiconductor electrodes.
a Pockels cover for a lossy dielectric can electrically control the reflection from the lossy dielectric in the mid-wavelenght and long-wavelength infrared regimes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Pockels covers provide a means of controlling the reflection of oblique light by a lossy dielectric backed by a metal, without depolarization, which is a challenge for the conventional electro-optic devices.
the reflectance of a dielectric slab backed a perfect electric conductor in the infrared regime can be electrically modulated by a Pockels cover.
a Pockels cover can control the reflectance of a lossy slab in both the mid- and long-wavelength infrared regimes.
